title: Pricing: Usage Smoothing and Multi-plan Quota Mapping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Large customers with bursty traffic are experiencing immediate overage charges and rate-limit throttles even when their weekly or monthly usage averages are within plan thresholds. At the same time, platform teams are asking for a single coherent mapping when customers subscribe to multiple plans (e.g., a base plan + add-on plan for embeddings) so usage attribution and billing reconciliation are deterministic.

Goal:
Design and specify a pricing/packaging behavior that smooths short-term spikes (usage smoothing), implements a deterministic multi-plan quota mapping strategy, and defines acceptance criteria and reconciliation rules for billing and ops. This should reduce surprise overage invoices and support predictable throttling policies while preserving cost controls.

Out of scope:
- Changes to token pricing tiers or list prices.
- Deep changes to the billing engine architecture (we will specify inputs/outputs for the billing team).

Success metrics:
- Reduction in customer support tickets flagged as "unexpected overages" by >= 60% in the first month after rollout (measured on pilot accounts).
- Reduction in Pager alerts due to sudden quota exhaustion by >= 40%.
- Billing reconciliation mismatch rate <= 0.1% for accounts using the multi-plan mapping model on pilot cohort.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Kapoor (owner)
- Billing & Finance: Marisa Chen
- Backend/Quota enforcement: Eng lead Daniel Reyes
- Console & UX: Priya Nambiar
- Customer Success: Omar Liu

High-level approach:
1) Usage smoothing: introduce a configurable smoothing window (default 5 minutes) and a short-term reserve buffer (soft-cap) that allows transient spikes without immediate overage; smoothing does not change metered usage for billing but delays throttle enforcement to the next enforcement tick. This is an operational control for latency-sensitive apps.
2) Multi-plan quota mapping: establish deterministic priority and split rules when multiple entitlements apply (e.g., plan-level quota, product-add-on quota, promo credits). Provide a deterministic mapping order and an API to preview which quota will be consumed.
3) Reconciliation contract: billing will receive both raw metered usage and a smoothing-adjusted enforcement log to perform invoicing and to offer a transparent customer-facing invoice line explaining "smoothing credit" where applicable.

Key user flows impacted:
- API request denied due to quota exhaustion: now returns an enriched error with active_quota_id, remaining_window_allowance, and smoothing_state.
- Console quota preview: customers can simulate a burst and see whether smoothing would have prevented a throttle or overage.

Operational controls and default values:
- smoothing_window_default: 300 seconds (configurable per-customer: 60–3600s)
- soft_cap_percentage_default: 20% of plan quota (can be zero for locked/platinum customers)
- enforcement_tick: every 60s for enforcement decisions

Implementation notes for Eng:
- Quota engine must emit two streams: raw_metered_events and enforcement_events. Enforcement_events are used by the rate limiter and include smoothing_state and applied_quota_id.
- Add DB mapping for multi-plan priority: integer priority + split rules (percent or first-fit).
- API additions: GET /v1/quota/preview, GET /v1/quota/active, and enriched 429 response headers/JSON.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New console dashboard: "Smoothing Effectiveness" showing prevented throttles, smoothing credits applied, and per-customer smoothing window.
- Billing dashboard: smoothing-adjusted totals vs raw metered totals.

Rollback conditions:
- Pilot accounts see >10% increase in billing disputes in first two billing cycles.
- Unacceptable latency introduced by enforcement pipeline (>200ms p95 increase on auth path).

Notes on legal/finance visibility:
- "Smoothing credits" are operationally neutral for revenue recognition but must be explicitly described on invoices as adjustments. Finance to confirm invoice wording and ledger treatment before release.
requirements: REQ-1: Smoothing window must be configurable per-customer and default to 300s.
REQ-2: Enforcement path must use smoothing-adjusted allowance and emit enforcement_events for auditability.
REQ-3: Multi-plan mapping must support three deterministic strategies: priority-first, proportional-split, and promo-consume-first.
REQ-4: API error responses for quota/throttle (429) must include active_quota_id, remaining_window_allowance, and smoothing_state fields.
REQ-5: Console must provide a quota preview simulation tool for customers and internal SEs.
REQ-6: Billing team must receive both raw_metered_events and enforcement_events for reconciliation; schema v2 to be agreed in dependency ticket.
REQ-7: Admin UI to toggle smoothing on/off per account and override soft_cap_percentage.
REQ-8: Default soft_cap_percentage is 20% but can be configured to 0/10/20/50 for special contracts.
REQ-9: All changes must include tracing hooks to attribute decisions in distributed traces for postmortems.
REQ-10: Customers must be able to opt-out of smoothing (explicit per-account opt-out via API/Console).
REQ-11: Audit logs must persist enforcement_events for 13 months for compliance and customer disputes.
REQ-12: Rate-limiter must maintain p99 enforcement latency <= 50ms added overhead on typical request path after optimization.
REQ-13: Backwards compatibility: existing customers not opted into smoothing must see no behavioral change by default unless enabled by billing or admin.
REQ-14: Provide a migration playbook for converting accounts from legacy multi-plan behavior to deterministic mapping with no invoice surprises.
REQ-15: Support per-route and per-model entitlements (e.g., text-gen vs embeddings) in multi-plan mapping logic.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Pilot cohort (10 customers across small/medium/large) enabled with smoothing shows >=60% fewer 'unexpected overage' tickets in first 30 days.
AC-2: Enforcement_events stream includes smoothing_state and applied_quota_id for 100% of throttle/enforcement decisions in pilot accounts.
AC-3: Billing receives raw_metered_events and enforcement_events and can reconcile invoices with mismatch <= 0.1% in pilot billing cycle.
AC-4: Console quota preview matches enforcement outcomes for simulated bursts in at least 95% of test cases (integration tests).
AC-5: API 429 responses include the new fields and SDKs updated to parse them; integration smoke tests pass in CI.
AC-6: Admin UI can toggle smoothing per-account and adjust soft_cap; the change takes effect within 60s and is visible in enforcement stream.
AC-7: Rollout does not increase p99 request path latency by more than 15% and adds <=200ms to worst-case auth/enforcement path; verified in perf tests.
AC-8: Feature flag gating exists to fully turn off smoothing platform-wide within a single deploy window.
AC-9: Finance legal has approved invoice wording for smoothing credits and billing training doc is published before GA.
AC-10: Playbook for dispute handling, including how to surface enforcement_events to SEs, is published and validated by CS team.
